I’ve been to different facilities, and this place stands out because they have passion, care, and they treat your goals like their own.

If you mind your business, focus, and show up for your workout, you will make progress. Iron Forge is full of serious people and pro trainers.

This facility was one of the closest I’ve seen to that feeling of community, passion, discipline and grit. I had a great time of growth and learning here, and I truly recommend it.

Only thing I’d say is sometimes maintenance takes a little longer, but nothing that ruins the experience. Overall, it’s a really good gym and the big Texas owners are good people and front desk it's welcoming too.

Front desk were really nice, shoutout to the person I chatted with. Some unique equipment I hadn't seen at other gyms. Came on a Monday after work (6PM), had plenty of open spaces so no wait. The classes looked like the biggest feature here, will definitely try a drop in class. Would recommend and come back if in the area.

Things that could be improved in my opinion: some plates don't appear consistent, aside from the different brands, the same brand ones can vary a little in size. Maybe more air circulation would be nice.

Things to note: The gym is 24/7, but for members, if you plan to drop in,  plan accordingly! You can also do a week-long pass too but was told it's most worth if you plan on actually dropping in multiple days. Day pass was $10.

I only come here for the Sunday open sparring/rolling sessions, and my experience has been great. The guys are extremely respectful and communicative. Since day one, it’s been a solid environment to work on technique and fight IQ.

Of course, the coach pushes some of his fighters, so certain rounds can get a little more intense — but that’s expected when you’re training in a mixed group of hobbyists, people who want to stay sharp, and fighters pursuing a career. I’m all for it.

It’s also the kind of place where, if someone is going a little too hard, you can simply communicate and ask them to tone it down. Everyone I’ve worked with has been more than respectful. And if you want more intense rounds, there are definitely some studs who will match your pace as long as you’re respectful. Nobody is there to start fights — everyone is there to train.

After reading some of the negative comments about the gym, you really have to take them with a grain of salt. Some people will complain about anything. It’s not the gym’s fault if someone didn’t read their contract or ask questions before signing. And it makes no sense to complain about cancelation fees that were clearly stated.

I’ve never experienced any aggression here. It’s a gym, not a ballet studio — you’re going to hear music, and you’re going to see people who are serious about fitness. As for equipment, they have everything you would need for Olympic lifting, bodybuilding, or general fitness. I can’t speak to pricing since I only come for sparring, but I can’t imagine it’s uncompetitive with the rest of Austin or the surrounding areas; otherwise, people wouldn’t keep coming.

I love the open mat community on Sundays and really enjoy being around guys who are competitive and ready to put in work. Plenty of young men could benefit from checking this place out, along with the coaches across their Muay Thai, MMA, and BJJ programs.

The gym seems cool at first, but the atmosphere quickly gets old. They have a severe lack of weights, and instead of addressing that, they enforce extreme rules. I was confronted by a regular member in a hostile way for forgetting to put back a couple of plates. First time in a month I’d forgotten to, and I’ve personally moved weights that weren’t racked there dozens of times myself. It’s a trivial part of gym life, and no one is perfect.

I’ve been working in gyms for nearly 20 years, and this was the first time I experienced such an awkward and unnecessary confrontation. Some of the equipment is decent, but most of it is lackluster. The environment feels toxic, especially compared to gyms like Gold’s or 24 Hour, and the price is too high, around $60/month when $45–50 would be more reasonable.

Awesome staff, amazing community, good equipment and a variety of options to workout all at a good price. I can't ask for much more and from what I hear this is just the start. Looking forward to seeing whats in store for this gym. A welcome addition to round rock, I definitely recommend!

Highly recommend. I will 100% be making this my new gym.

P.S. HUGE bonus for being able to pay for the membership in bulk. I wish more gyms did this.

One of the best gyms I have ever been to! So far NOT PACKED! Even on peak hours. Which I love! Staff is so nice and helpful. Gym is clean and lots of equipment to pick from. I signed up the first day. I definitely recommend. Gym is safe & very clean. You also get this vibe or atmosphere that keeps you motivated!

Really clean and loads of equipment, also really top notch panatta machines.... Could easily be a 5 star gym.... The absolute plague of influencers and tripods is what ruins it for me.  I was here a month before I went back to my old gym.  The sheer volume of influencers taking up space and equipment, filming with tripods, conducting interviews, etc. just isn't worth the hassle.  I usually get in around 930pm and it was still an issue. May be a great gym for the kids... But not for an old head like me.

This would have been 5 stars for everything a gym should be. Great equipment, great people, decent value for the cost of the membership, and not too crowded. A lot of the equipment here is Panatta branded stuff, so they are really high quality machines. People were nice, plenty of friendly people and faces.

Unfortunately, whoever they have partnered with that manages the whole memberships/contracts section of the business completely tarnished the few months I had been there.

When a business says, "Sorry, because you cancelled your membership 12 days before your next renewal cycle instead of 14, we are going to have to charge you another FULL MONTH of membership (which isn't cheap by the way). Not to mention I hadn't even been using the last couple weeks of my current month of membership because I had moved. But that also doesn't matter I guess. On top of that they also charge you $20 dollars for canceling online instead of in-person. So just to cancel your membership, you are looking at 80 dollars, even if you cancel before the next month renews. And I specifically stated I was moving addresses, so I would no longer be there. Then they hit you with the, "But it was in the contract!" which just makes my blood boil with how gym businesses get away with that type of behavior.

I sent out an email similar to what I said above, and they told me they did me a favor by not "renewing next month" but instead, it will go out to collections and ruin my credit instead. So sure, if you do want to go to this gym, just make sure you ask them to give you a special provision that you will not agree to the garbage terms they provide you.

Hopefully they get rid of whoever they partnered with 3rd party wise so it can continue being a good gym without their help, because I can promise you they are definitely not helping.

*UPDATE* I found out that now I currently "owe" over 200 dollars. This is because when you cancel your gym membership, they count that as "requesting" to cancel your membership. They will not stop charging you for your membership UNTIL you pay their extortion fees and any remaining balance. So you will continue to pay months after cancelling. Some really great business practices here!!!
